SCF #46 / DEVELOPER TOOLING / OPEN TRACK

Stellar Discovery
Trust Layer

From an approved payment
to complete, useful work.

TokenJunkieLabs requests USD 38,000 equivalent in XLM for 400 prospective delivery hours over 150 days from actual award acceptance. The work installs a useful paid Stellar service with two independently operated merchants, two independent buyer operators and the same selected operation through two independently operated facilitators.

The product is open-source, self-hostable merchant and buyer tooling. It carries an approved API request, dataset or paid MCP tool through native settlement, complete useful output, fulfillment and operating handover. The merchant controls its source and terms. The buyer controls its keys, request and spending. Another engineer can reopen the installation and recover unfinished work.

The working development baseline comprises 18 distinct team-operated purchases totaling 411,000 stroops, or 0.0411 native testnet XLM, with network fees recorded separately. The funded milestones establish independent customer operation, repeated use and production receiving from that baseline.

    Project and requested outcome

    TokenJunkieLabs builds open-source, self-hostable software that carries a paid API, dataset or agent operation through to completed customer work. A merchant publishes an authorized resource; a buyer approves the exact request and total spending, pays through Stellar, and receives the complete result in its application. The merchant retains the offer, fulfillment and accounting. Another engineer can restore the installation and continue its original work.

    We request $38,000 for 400 prospective development and technical integration hours over 150 days from actual award acceptance. The funded outcome is two independently operated merchant services used by two independent buyer operators:

    • Day 30: both services installed with their authorized sources, receiving applications and accountable operators.
    • Day 90: at least ten useful testnet purchases in total across the two independent buyers during seven consecutive days, with both merchants represented; the same useful service operates through two independent facilitators.
    • Day 150: both merchants live on mainnet, with at least thirty useful purchases in total across the two independent buyers during fourteen consecutive days, both buyers returning on another UTC day, and completed recovery and independent maintainer handover.

    The working product supplies the architecture, payments and source-to-customer foundation. The six packages below fund the selected installations' remaining source adapters, receiving integration, deployment, monitoring and recovery. Reusable improvements return to the public product; completed pre-award work remains the starting point.

    Customer problem, need and adoption

    Our initial users are recurring API/data-service operators and the agencies integrating their services into customer applications. The commissioning payer buys implementation and handover; the merchant earns resource receipts; the independent buyer purchases useful output. These roles may belong to different organizations.

    A paid response must become a usable customer result: every required page or file, the correct population and period, original units and types, and an output that opens in the receiving application. An interrupted request also needs a clear financial and delivery outcome. These requirements are especially important when an agent makes several paid requests to complete one task.

    We support two recurring installation patterns:

    Customer taskAccepted output
    Receive a new economic or operational reporting period, then compare it with the previous edition.Complete report and underlying selection, retaining units, periods, source editions and review decisions.
    Run an approved typed query or acquire a refreshed dataset.Every agreed page/file, with the exact request, source selection, aggregate cost and merchant record.

    The two funded installations and agreements remain to be selected. Current conversations refine the customer and payer model. CoCart’s founder asked how introductions, implementation fees, contracting and platform support would work; our October 12 proposal assigns introductions to CoCart, implementation and handover to TokenJunkieLabs under a direct customer contract, and a written referral arrangement. Veridex invited our existing buyer CLI into its testnet cohort and reported no third-party testing budget. Our latest reply proposes a paid buyer-integration pilot, partner funding or a specifically valued reciprocal workshare with agreed deliverables and usage rights. Blockscout expressed interest and reported no integration budget; Nansen declined. The detailed customer and commercial plan carries the corresponding installation roles and workshare scope.

    Each selected workorder will name the payer, source owner, merchant, independent buyer, integration and receiving engineers, host and acceptance owner. It will specify the authorized population/period/query, useful output, advertised paid unit, aggregate spending limit and responsibility for hosting and purchases. An installed baseline and a later genuinely needed period, edition or query establish recurring demand. Source permission, operator availability and the complete customer task are settled before its deployed work begins.

    The delivered economic, Timescale, aid-data and scientific-array applications provide concrete candidates for these two patterns. Existing proposed workshares retain their original source, effort, fees and customer conditions in the detailed application. For example, the GeoRobotix observation-source proposal is $9,600 / 72 engineering hours / twelve active business days, with two $4,800 milestones. Its first offer was sent on October 13 at 00:05:31 UTC; delivery starts after source selection, access and the receiving environment are ready. Its reusable illustrative-source workflow has completed review, query/export, separate receiving and cold reopen. The commercial case has separately completed scope planning, independent receiving and the maintained Installation intake; its eight engineering workorders remain planned. Customer installation, live collection and the paid Stellar service remain prospective.

    The environmental commissioning programme makes that selection practical. Five original offers cover complete laboratory reissues, a client import, a monitoring study and a KiWIS programme. Their retained plans contain 25 phases /206 planned commercial hours /$24,600 in proposed implementation fees, with $12,300 at agreed starts and $12,300 at accepted handovers. Those are sent proposals; no customer acceptance or revenue is recorded for this cohort. Four shipped Installation profiles translate the original scopes into source selection, scientific review, full output and independent receiving. Two laboratories share one technical profile while preserving separate case, plan and acceptance identities. The installed operating course lets the engineer open each original workshare, agree the customer’s actual source and receiving environment, and select a later useful delivery or reporting window. The two grant-funded installations remain independently selected.

    The purchase target follows actual work. Two buyers making one purchase per weekday would produce only twenty purchases in fourteen days. The chosen T3 work must therefore require at least thirty distinct useful paid requests across both buyers and merchants. Advertised pages can be separate purchases within one complete task; replay, reopening and cached use retain the original purchase. The existing Customer-use Calendar links the saved Installation, buyers, complete tasks and funding groups to the original purchase observations.

    TokenJunkieLabs earns separately agreed implementation and care fees. Merchants retain resource revenue and implementation partners retain customer relationships. Each adaptation, delivery hour and support obligation is allocated once between the grant and commissioned work.

    Why Stellar and what we contribute

    Stellar supplies authorization and settlement for the selected purchase. In the existing x402 Exact flow, the buyer signs token-transfer authorization binding payer, recipient, atomic amount and expiration. A facilitator submits it on the selected network; fee sponsorship can cover the transaction fee. We use existing Stellar SDKs and token contracts.

    Our application binds that transfer to the exact HTTP request or MCP tool/arguments, selected source, payment option, complete customer output and fulfillment history. The buyer controls wallet authority and total spend; the merchant controls source access, pricing and fulfillment.

    The ecosystem already supplies substantial infrastructure. Stellar's x402 client libraries handle payment challenges, Soroban authorization and signed retries; the Stellar CLI supplies the signing identity. Facilitators verify and settle, and Bazaar describes discoverable resources. ApiCharge's published proxy/access-grant approach provides typed paid access and retained purchased service levels. MPP Router provides paid proxy access, request-ID response caching and signed job polling. Our proposed Open Track contribution is a reusable way to keep an entire paid customer task coherent across those components: the reviewed source and query, aggregate approval, distinct native transfers, every agreed page/file, editable output, interrupted-delivery recovery, accounting and independent maintenance. The application retains the original relationship among those records when a provider, source edition or receiving operator changes. The two customer installations develop the remaining source/consumer and deployment joins and return reusable improvements to that public workflow. Open Track fit rests on this technical and customer-operation contribution and its measured usefulness; the selected track remains subject to the issuer’s invitation and review.

    The programme makes that contribution measurable. It installs two independent services and buyers, operates the same useful service through two testnet facilitators, and carries both merchants into recurring mainnet use. The two-provider comparison holds the service, schema, source population and useful output constant. Existing catalogs do not by themselves establish this compatibility: the retained Vellar/Periplo comparison found no shared seller/route identity, so explicit registration and integration of the same service is part of the funded work.

    Stellar x402 · Stellar agent payment guide · ApiCharge protocol · MPP Router. The detailed application retains the full business and technical comparison.

    Defined architecture and operating behavior

    The architecture is defined and implemented across six components:

    ComponentResponsibility
    Merchant workspaceSelect authorized source/query, schema, output, price and limits. Retain separately reviewed source and terms changes or withdrawal.
    HTTP or MCP resourcePreserve types, nulls, pagination, keys, units, time basis and snapshot/live semantics. Use customer-controlled source credential references.
    Buyer approval and budgetApprove exact method/tool, arguments, scope and payment option; match the challenge and schema before signing. Reserve aggregate task spending alongside per-payment limits.
    Stellar settlementUse the reviewed network, asset, recipient, amount, expiry and fee policy. Reconcile the native transfer through independent RPC observation.
    Delivery and accountingRetain all agreed outputs, original attempts, accepted fulfillment, notifications and acknowledgments. Preserve prepaid selection/consumption, usage periods, prices, invoices and receipts.
    Recovery and receivingKeep approval, settlement and delivery states distinct; reconcile the original dispatch after an uncertain response. Restore source, configuration, history and files for another authorized engineer.

    Catalog browsing retains the full selected page, offer and payment alternative. Advertised schemas guide explicit request inputs; the saved intent contains the concrete request, body and spending limit. The Request Collections input library accepts original catalogue and body files from desktop or phone, resumes interrupted transfers, and retains exact inputs privately. Buyers select the actual offer and advertised terms, then use saved plans and named periods through the existing review and spending controls. Recovery and downloads reopen that same service workspace. A prepaid call retains its selected pass and consumed allowance when defaults change. MPP Charge retains its own authorization and recovery lifecycle.

    The prepaid commissioning desk carries that installation work from reviewed checkout, payment, allowance and host settings to the original native preparation, generated source and Applications setup document. The merchant retains its publication; the customer receives the complete handoff and opens the original workspace. A portable editable document carries those exact results and configuration history to the next engineer. This shipped commissioning source supports the first thirty days of installation work; its executed authored source course adds no purchase or independent buyer to the development baseline.

    The complete financial walkthrough continues the original merchant and customer from the useful paid result through quote/invoice review, actual Stellar or bank receiving, dated allocations, refunds, bank reconciliation and customer close. Its browser, HTTP, CLI and 46 receivables MCP actions share the original accounting workspace. Customer/order setup, usage captures, reviewed service periods, saved closing cycles, corrections and complete handovers retain their own records. Purchase principal, fees, commercial valuation, separately issued obligations and later service activity keep their respective identities.

    Node.js supplies browser, CLI, typed-client and MCP interfaces; source and receiving applications also use Python/SQLite and PHP/WordPress/WooCommerce. Each facilitator has explicit network, asset, recipient, signer and fee policies. T2 configures two compatible testnet operators for the same service; T3 deploys each merchant's reviewed mainnet configuration. Existing SDKs/contracts remain the payment foundation. The selected x402 Exact integration uses existing Stellar token contracts. Its public release identifies the upstream contract and SDK source, versions and licenses alongside the maintained integration code; any funded modifications to contract code will be included under compatible open-source terms. The existing unified development guide collects the architecture and diagram, interface ownership, roadmap, development artifacts and native acceptance/recovery plan. The application states the technical design and acceptance outcomes here; that guide supplies the full development material.

    Named delivery and financial operation. The existing Grant Operations workspace gives lead, finance, reviewer and contributor staff individual sign-ins and assigned cases. Work, invoices, observed payments and corrections retain their original records and named actors; the complete installation carries those records and source into independent restoration.

    Working product and demonstrated results

    The working product demonstrates three customer outcomes. Its development baseline is 18 distinct team-operated testnet purchases totaling 411,000 stroops / 0.0411 native XLM, with fees separate. Independent customer deployments and mainnet use are the funded next stage.

    Complete recurring dataset receiving. All 830 original OData Orders passed through typed collection, saved SQL, a report, a two-sheet workbook and independent analytical receiving. Three subscription editions, original-request replay, independent publisher/customer restores and restored-publisher continuation completed. The same source definition produced zero row changes, retained as the actual result. The separate managed selection built and loaded all twelve entry points; managed preparation/adoption and Review → Start → receive → Stop → reopen remain to be operated on that completed customer edition.

    A real Stellar purchase with a useful output. Two 10,000-stroop purchases completed one 144-row Queens HPD customer task, received as pages of 100 and 44 rows and reopened as CSV/JSONL with original source and accounting. A separate 50,000-stroop purchase returned 100 rows and fourteen columns, retained its original truncation flag, and reopened with signing disconnected and in another directory. Reviewers can inspect the original acquisition record, reviewer operating guide and 3:32 product/team film.

    Independent restoration and handover. The OData receiver restored and continued the original subscription. Saved prepaid passes preserved each call’s selected pass and consumed allowance through replay and cold receiving. The OpenLineage customer operation let another engineer reopen accepted measurements, reports and history. Installation, recurring requests, bank statements and customer service closing retain their original operating and financial records. The complete Resource Review operation also received a conflicting reviewer return, applied the reviewed resolution, exported its full journal and continued editing after independent receiving without the original source files. Twelve desktop and phone views completed with no recorded page or console errors. Its merged customer continuation connects the Python entry, exact comparison and originating return to that full review.

    Discovery also has a measured baseline against the actual 27-resource Vellar testnet catalog: schema-aware ranking retrieved all 31 declared query-resource relationships versus 22 previously, with matching direct/indexed results across 33 queries. The complete comparison retains that source-based measurement.

    The merged IATI operating-procedure component adds editable customer plans and complete analyst receiving. The detailed product companion preserves the full product inventory, source populations, operating outcomes and remaining deployment steps. Selected customer source/roles, deployed purchasing/recovery and production handover remain within the existing T1, T2 and T3 packages.

    The Human Services Directory has also completed its original native source-to-referral and independent receiving operation: twenty mapped fields, three resulting FHIR resources, retained warnings and service-selection classification, an explicit referral join and the full editable customer workspace. Its merged Operating Plans and declared-relationship operator extend the same source and customer workflow. The Directory chapter connects that delivered foundation to the existing source-specific T1 installation, T2 paid operation and T3 recurring-use/handover packages.

    The Installation receiver-to-owner workflow also completed its full team-operated receiving: a receiver’s named observations return to the owner for explicit KEEP/APPLY decisions, changed criteria require a fresh review, and the next Installation edition remains editable. The original model/CLI, typed HTTP/MCP, desktop and phone Page, independent receiving and cold reopen all completed at revision 3. This demonstrates the handover and correction mechanism that T1 authority/handover and T3 recovery will configure for the two future customer installations.

    Named-staff operating result. The completed staff workflow operated six profiles, three work records and two example invoices through contribution, review, payment and correction. Fifteen desktop/mobile browser views completed without errors. The independently restored installation retained and verified all 421 source files, and reopened the original business history after a cold restart.

    Bryce owns delivery, source/release decisions and tranche submissions. Each workorder assigns integration, merchant/source, independent buyer, receiving/support and acceptance responsibilities. One person can hold several roles; the two merchant and two buyer independence requirements follow accountable organizations or people across wallets and agents.

    Receiving covers the original source selection, complete reports/data and backups, an independent restore, managed Stop/reopen, and a later-edition comparison on the same keys, fields and population. Genuine unchanged data remains unchanged.

    The day-150 release includes the saved product plan and Runtime handoff, dependency/license inventory, installation/upgrade instructions, configuration references and customer-state receiving procedure. It identifies the host owner, maintainer, primary/backup responders, service-cost owner and care scope. Updates start from deployed source, preserve resource identity and buyer/state records, review route/schema/payment changes and drain admitted work before switching traffic. Rollback preserves later purchases and output; restore reconciles operations after the backup point. Compatibility changes and migration instructions return to the maintained component, with open support cases retained in the handover.

    The grant funds prospective Stellar-integrated development. Completed pre-award implementation, sales, general operations, purchase principal and network fees have separate funding. Existing compute is the starting resource; incremental service reserve and hosted Actions budget are $0. Each adaptation is assigned once to a funded package or separate commercial workshare. Completed reusable work is reconciled with the remaining estimate at award.

    For an environmental installation selected by the grant, the original workorder allocates the remaining customer-source adapter and complete receiving join to T1, facilitator/payment deployment and operating recovery to T2, and recurring mainnet use plus independent maintenance to T3. The shipped profile, source preparer and completed pre-award code remain its starting product. Each selected phase records its original commercial plan, assigned engineer, funding source and acceptance owner before work is scheduled. If a commissioned scope and a funded package use the same improvement, the case assigns its delivery hours once and retains the resulting source for both workflows. The five proposed commercial workshares retain their own fees, milestones and delivery clocks. They add no hours or amount to the existing 400-hour /$38,000 /150-day grant request.
